question.text: Starting at time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> from the origin with speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, a particle follows a two-dimensional trajectory in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>y</mi></math> plane so that its coordinates are related by the equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math> components of its acceleration are denoted by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>y</mi></msub></math>, respectively. Then

options.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> implies that when the particle is at the origin, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>y</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>

at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></math> the particle's velocity points in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-direction

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> implies that at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mo>,</mo></math> the angle between the particle's velocity and the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> axis is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo></math>
